text:
harper: Heads-up: CloudDocs (large doc-editing customer) requested a hardened catalog onboarding lane: 99th pctl latency commitments, an option to pin model versions for 9-18 months, and explicit migration tooling. They're asking what we can promise and what we'd charge.
diego: Need to separate three asks: perf SLA, pin duration, and migration guarantees. Perf SLA implies reserved infra + capacity planning. Pin implies model freeze or controlled rollouts. Migration tooling is PS + automation.
sylvie: Quick feasibility: 99th pctl under 200ms for their workload (avg seq ~256, bursty weekends) looks possible on Dedicated with pre-warmed cache and batching tuned; hosted wouldn't be safe. We'll need a nightly priming job and a cache-warm SLA window.
ron: Questions: do they need bit-compatibility (exact outputs) or quality parity? That affects how we handle fallback variants. Also, do they want an on-prem/private deployment?
harper: They prefer hosted but will consider Dedicated if price is reasonable. They asked for quality parity with <2% regression on their evaluation prompts. No bit-for-bit requirement.
infra-bot: Canary scheduled: priming-run v1 -> staging at 2025-11-05T08:00Z
diego: Pricing sketch: pin 9mo = +20% model premium, 12mo = +30%, 18mo = +45%. Dedicated reserved capacity is billed separately (monthly commit). Migration assistance: fixed 40-hour onboarding block + hourly PS thereafter or an optional fixed migration credit.
sylvie: From product side we need: 1) benchmark spec (latency tail, throughput, cost curve) 2) customer prompt set run and regression check 3) rollout plan (canary -> staged rollout + auto-rollback on quality drop) 4) cache warm policy and pre-warm window.
tess: Legal/strategy: deprecation window should be longer for pinned customers. Propose baseline 120d notice, extendable to 180/270d for paid tiers. Also require customers to opt into migration assistance; limit liability & define "reasonable effort."
harper: I'll draft a concise spec to present to CloudDocs: include recommended infra, expected cost delta, and minimum acceptance tests. Can we include a sample perf command they can run?
sylvie: Yes, give them a lightweight harness command:
```
# local microbenchmark against our public api
./redwood-bench --endpoint=https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen \
  --qps 500 --seq 256 --duration 180 --concurrency 24
```
ron: Ops note: implement an SLO dashboard tile for pinned accounts showing cache-hit ratio, tail latency, and per-route rollback triggers. Also record pre-warm windows so we can audit.
diego: Action items: sylvie write benchmark spec + harness; ron scope dashboard + rollback hooks; tess draft deprecation and PS language; harper assemble commercial proposal and meeting with CloudDocs. Sync Friday 9am.
harper: Thanks — will add to the handbook and ping sales.
